record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.context_brief: Disk rigidity with few periodic points
record.original_question: Let f be a smooth Lebesgue-measure-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed unit disk D^2 = {z ∈ C : |z| ≤ 1} with only finitely many periodic points. Must f be smoothly C^∞-conjugate to the rigid rotation r_α(z) = e^{2πiα} z for some angle α?

evidence.quote: We also ask the similar question for D2 ={z ∈ C,|z| ≤1}. When f is Lebesgue measure preserving and f has a ﬁnite number of periodic points is f C∞ -conjugated to rα ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}^2 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| \le 1\}$ denote the closed unit disk, equipped with Lebesgue measure. For $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, let $r_\alpha : \mathbb{D}^2 \to \mathbb{D}^2$ be the rigid rotation $r_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$.

Suppose $f : \mathbb{D}^2 \to \mathbb{D}^2$ is a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism that preserves Lebesgue measure and has only finitely many periodic points. Must there exist $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ and a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $h : \mathbb{D}^2 \to \mathbb{D}^2$ such that $h \circ f \circ h^{-1} = r_\alpha$?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was located. The analogous rigidity question for area-preserving disk diffeomorphisms with finitely many periodic points appears to remain open; related literature addresses mixing properties and Calabi-invariant inequalities but does not establish smooth conjugacy to a rigid rotation under the stated hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: On mixing diffeomorphisms of the disk
status_evidence.snippet: Area preserving smooth diffeomorphisms of the disc with zero topological entropy are never topologically mixing.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on disk diffeomorphisms address mixing rather than smooth conjugacy to rotation, indicating the rigidity question remains unsettled.

status_evidence.title: Jean-Christophe Yoccoz and the theory of circle diffeomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth conjugacy of circle diffeomorphisms to rotations under Diophantine conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The circle analog is well-understood (Herman-Yoccoz), but the disk version is a separate, open question.
